sites.kf: Parks Canada: on 6 Dec 1917 the explosives-laden SS Mont-Blanc and SS Imo collided in Halifax Harbour, causing a massive explosion, a tidal wave and fires; some 2,000 people died and thousands more were wounded; widespread destruction of homes; a national historic event commemorated at Fort Needham Memorial Park.

src.t: Parks Canada, 'Halifax Explosion National Historic Event'

sites.n: Bedford Magazine explosion (RCN magazine, Bedford Basin)
cas: Displaced: thousands of residents of Dartmouth and north Halifax left their homes
sites.kf: Halifax Municipal Archives: 18-19 July 1945; ammunition from ships being refitted for the Pacific was stored at the Bedford Magazine; a fire at the magazine's jetty set off a series of explosions through the night into the next morning; thousands evacuated; one patrolman killed and many others injured.

src.t: Halifax Municipal Archives, 'Bedford Magazine Explosion, July 18-19, 1945' (virtual exhibit)
Library and Archives Canada, RCN file 'Ammunition - Explosions and accidents - Explosion and fire July 1945 - RCN Magazine Bedford Basin' (catalogue record; read in a search summary)

sites.n: San José Island old chemical weapons (Pearl Islands)
sites.ty: Republic of Panama; OPCW verification · chemical munitions (old chemical weapons)
sites.kf: OPCW: Panama informed the Secretariat that all eight declared old chemical weapons had been destroyed; an OPCW inspection team observed the process. Panama (EC-86/NAT.20): OPCW-Panama agreement on inspections on San José Island dated 12 Jul 2017; OPCW technical verification team on the island 13-25 Sep 2017.

src.t: OPCW EC-86/DG.32, Director-General's opening statement to EC-86 (Oct 2017)
OPCW EC-86/NAT.20, Statement by Panama to the 86th Executive Council (10 Oct 2017)

sites.n: Former US Canal Zone firing ranges (UXO) transferred to Panama
sites.ty: Former US military ranges (Canal Area) · unexploded ordnance
sites.kf: US State Dept (Hidden Killers 2001): US military records indicate that since 1984 UXO killed seven Panamanians and one US soldier, all from trespassing into restricted range impact areas; after US clearance the US turned over 7,675 acres to Panama.

src.t: U.S. Department of State, 'Hidden Killers 2001: The World's Landmine Problem' (archived 2001-2009 site)

sites.ty: former gold mine; arsenic trioxide waste · Operator: Government of Canada (CIRNAC) custodian; GNWT co-proponent
sites.kf: CIRNAC: roasting arsenopyrite ore created about 237,000 t of arsenic trioxide dust (about 79% arsenic trioxide) stored in 14 underground chambers and stopes (11 chambers and 5 stopes exist); no new arsenic trioxide since Royal Oak Mines went bankrupt in 1999; frozen-block containment chosen; no 'walk-away' solution - water treatment and monitoring required indefinitely. GNWT: mine operated 1948-2004; 56 options considered (2001-2003); remediation expected complete by 2038.

src.t: CIRNAC (Government of Canada), 'Arsenic trioxide and underground issues at Giant Mine'
Government of the Northwest Territories, 'Giant Mine Remediation Project'

sites.n: Faro Mine Complex (Faro and Vangorda), Yukon
sites.ty: abandoned open-pit lead-zinc mine · Operator: Government of Canada (CIRNAC)
sites.kf: CIRNAC: once the largest open-pit lead-zinc mine in the world; site spans 25 km2 near the town of Faro; left 70 million t of tailings and 320 million t of waste rock that leach metals and acid; abandoned in 1998; Type II site under the Yukon devolution agreement (2003); since 2018 Canada assumed all responsibility; 'stabilize in place' approach selected in 2009; care and maintenance with water collection and treatment.

src.t: CIRNAC, 'Faro Mine Remediation Project'
PSPC (Government of Canada) backgrounder 'Faro Mine Remediation Project' (Feb 2022) (page could not be opened; read in a search summary)

sites.n: Port Radium mine, Great Bear Lake
sites.ty: former radium, uranium and silver mine · Operator: Government of Canada (CIRNAC); CNSC regulates
sites.kf: CIRNAC: on the eastern shore of Great Bear Lake, 440 km north of Yellowknife and 265 km east of Délı̨nę; mined for radium from 1932, uranium early 1940s-1960s, silver 1960s-1982; remediation completed 2008 per the Canada-Délı̨nę Uranium Table; land-use permit closed 2013, CNSC continues to regulate; residual risks: low-level radiation (capped tailings), metals in soil and surface water, hydrocarbons at Silver Point.

src.t: CIRNAC, 'Port Radium'
INAC Contaminants and Remediation Directorate / Canada-Déline Uranium Table, 'Port Radium Mine Remediation Plan' (2005, Sahtu Land and Water Board registry S06D-004) (read in a search summary)

sites.n: Elliot Lake decommissioned uranium mines and tailings management areas
sites.ty: decommissioned uranium mines; tailings management areas · Operator: Rio Algom Ltd. and Denison Mines Inc. (CNSC licensees)
sites.kf: CNSC: 12 decommissioned uranium mine sites and 10 tailings management areas in and around Elliot Lake; all brought into production 1955-1958; five shut by 1970; decommissioning from 1992 lasting about a decade; all sites substantially decommissioned (capped/blocked, demolished, revegetated). CNSC 2008: low-grade ore (<0.1% U3O8) with pyrite and radium-226; acid-generating tailings; dry covers at Lacnor, Nordic, Pronto and Stanrock need active water treatment; water covers at Quirke, Panel, Stanleigh, Spanish American and Denison.

src.t: Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission, 'Uranium mines and mills waste'
CNSC, Joint Convention report (Oct 2008), Annex 8 'Inactive Uranium Mines and Mills Tailings Management Areas'
Denison Mines / Rio Algom (licensees), 'Serpent River Watershed Cycle 4 (2010-2014) State of the Environment Report' (read in a search summary)

sites.kf: Westray Mine Public Inquiry: at 5:20 am on 9 May 1992 the Westray mine at Plymouth, just east of Stellarton, Pictou County, exploded, instantly killing the 26 miners working there; the Commissioner was appointed by Order in Council on 15 May 1992; report (Nov 1997) concluded the disaster was predictable and therefore preventable.

src.t: Westray Mine Public Inquiry (Justice K. Peter Richard), 'The Westray Story: A Predictable Path to Disaster', Executive Summary (Nov 1997), Province of Nova Scotia

sites.n: Pasta de Conchos coal mine explosion (Mina 8)
sites.kf: STPS (19 Feb 2009): the explosion of 19 Feb 2006 in Mina 8, Unidad Pasta de Conchos, municipality of San Juan de Sabinas, Coahuila, killed 65 mine workers.

src.t: Secretaría del Trabajo y Previsión Social (STPS), informe 'A tres años del accidente en la mina Pasta de Conchos' (19 Feb 2009)

sites.n: Buenavista del Cobre acidified copper-sulfate spill (Bacanuchi and Sonora rivers)
sites.ty: copper mine leachate spill · Operator: Buenavista del Cobre, S.A. de C.V. and/or Minera México
sites.kf: PROFEPA: spill of almost 40,000 m3 of acidified copper-sulfate leachate detected at 10:00 on 6 Aug 2014 entering the Bacanuchi river (Sonora river tributary); inspection act of 8 Aug 2014; criminal complaint filed with the PGR environmental unit for crimes under Art. 414 of the Federal Penal Code.

src.t: PROFEPA, 'Presenta PROFEPA denuncia penal contra responsables de derrame en río Bacanuchi' (Aug 2014)

sites.n: Marlin gold mine, San Miguel Ixtahuacán / Sipacapa
sites.ty: closed gold-silver mine · Operator: Glamis Gold, then Goldcorp (Oct 2006 - May 2017); Newmont since 2019
sites.kf: Newmont (2023): Marlin was owned and operated by Glamis Gold, then by Goldcorp from Oct 2006 until May 2017 when it ceased operating; Newmont bought Goldcorp in 2019 when Marlin was already in closure; physical reclamation completed late 2020; post-closure commitments continue.

sites.n: Jamaica bauxite mining and alumina red-mud (bauxite residue) disposal
sites.ty: bauxite mining and alumina refining · Operator: Industry; monitored by the Jamaica Bauxite Institute for NEPA
